newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU assembly demands sanctions against Renault.
newsitem.headline: EU assembly demands sanctions against Renault.

text.p: The European Parliament on Wednesday urged the European Union to penalise car maker Renault for its decision to close a plant in Belgium without first consulting and informing its workers.

Renault's "inadmissible" decision to close the Vilvoorde plant, with the loss of 3,100 jobs, totally disregarded EU laws on worker consultation and collective redundancies, Euro-MPs said in a resolution.
The European Commission and the Netherlands, as president of the Council of Ministers, should do everything in their power to reverse the decision, the non-binding resolution continued.

The EU assembly said Renault had shown "arrogance and disdain for the most fundamental rules of social consultation", and the EU needed swingeing sanctions to prevent companies from riding roughshod over EU worker protection laws in this way.
Euro-MPs echoed the concerns of trade unionists from Renault's Belgian, French, Spanish and Portuguese plants, who on Wednesday predicted worse was to come.

"The closure of Vilvoorde may just be the first sign. All employers in Europe are worst off because it could happen to them and it's something that is going to happen again," Hendrik Vermeersch, from Vilvoorde, told a news conference at the parliament.
Euro-MPs said collective redundancy was not necessarily the only option at Vilvoorde and Renault should work with its employees to find an alternative solution.

EU governments must also stop trying to lure multinationals away from other EU countries by offering them tax concessions and subsidies whose social costs would have to be borne by neighbouring member states, the parliament's resolution said.
